clue.text: European articles assembled for trial, reluctantly

parts.note: un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite one
un is a French indefinite article and der a German definite one
pro means in favour of, for
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Bits of European grammar are gathered for a hearing, though nobody is keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Two foreign articles, UN (French) and DER (German), come from one phrase; 'assembled' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something while objecting means doing it grudgingly, against one's will.

clue.text: Exalt — university has to exalt

parts.note: to praise is to exalt or glorify

explanation.surface: A university has a duty to glorify things.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise up or elevate in honour is to glorify, an archaic synonym.

clue.text: Section removed from ground by club

definitions.text: Section removed from ground by club

parts.words: Section removed from ground by club
parts.note: reads like a sports team losing part of its stadium, but describes the turf a golf club gouges out on a swing

explanation.surface: A sports club has part of its stadium taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's iron often cuts a chunk of turf from the fairway with each stroke.

clue.text: Comfort politician about article that shows how the land lies

definitions.text: that shows how the land lies

parts.note: relief is comfort or ease

indicators.note: the politician's letters go around the article, so it sits inside them

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Consoling a politician about some newspaper piece that reveals the true state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside MP; 'how the land lies' looks like the idiom for a situation but is literal terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of chart models hills and valleys in raised form, showing the terrain's contours.

clue.text: Screw up and repeat assignment of prizes

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder or guard

explanation.surface: Botch things and run the prize draw again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw up' looks like 'make a mess of'; in fact Screw is the prison guard and 'up' turns him backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizes are often assigned by a draw, so holding another draw is doing it again.

clue.text: Stocky pupils found among the lower classes?

definitions.text: pupils found among the lower classes?
definitions.meaning: playfully, the stream of dim pupils in a school's lower sets, read as two words

explanation.surface: Sturdy children seem to end up in the bottom streams at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into thick (dim) and set (a class grouped by ability), a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocky person is broad and heavily built, sturdy in frame.

clue.text: Name of saint associated with cathedral put up

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A saint's name is linked with a cathedral that has been erected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ELY to YLE. Ely, a small city in eastern England, is a crossword staple for 'cathedral'.
explanation.definitionFit: A title or form of address one is called by, as in 'styled Duke of York'.

clue.text: Dishearted 5, all below target

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Dishearted 5, all below target (8)': TEE + TOTAL is clear but 'Dishearted 5' is garbled OCR with no visible definition, and no search gives the printed text

clue.text: Shy little bird seen around lake

indicators.note: the bird's letters are seen surrounding the lake's letter

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A timid small bird is spotted near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' puts L inside FINCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to start back or recoil, as a horse does in fear.

clue.text: Snarl from composer

explanation.surface: A growl from a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads that tangle form a knot or snarl; the noun names that mess.

clue.text: Lead Sybil astray — she receives proposal

indicators.note: going astray, the letters wander out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misleads Sybil, a woman about to be asked to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges LEAD SYBIL. The old song has the suitor begging 'Daisy, Daisy, give me your answer, do'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the music-hall song the singer asks Daisy to marry him on a bicycle made for two.

clue.text: Unaware kind heart is broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and put back together in another order

explanation.surface: Someone oblivious has their kindly heart shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is broken' rearranges KIND HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uninformed is being left without light on the matter, the idiom for ignorance.

clue.text: College announced what courses should be

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the word's sound is what counts

parts.note: Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A college declares what its programmes of study should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' looks academic, after College, but means courses of a meal. ETON, a famous English boarding school, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses of a meal are meant to be consumed, so they should be devoured.

clue.text: Puzzle about morning drink taken by English

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the morning-and-drink run is read backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is morning
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning an early drink that an Englishman downs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AMGIN into NIGMA, which follows E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling or mysterious that cannot be explained is a riddle.

clue.text: Implements made of metal that's rendered narrow in the middle

indicators.note: the recast letters go into the middle of the 'that is' abbreviation

parts.note: i.e., id est, means 'that is'

indicators.note: rendered means made into something else, so the letters are recast

explanation.surface: Tools forged from metal that has been thinned at the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for i.e. (id est); 'rendered' recasts the clue's 'narrow' as RONWAR, and 'in the middle' sets it between those two letters. 'narrow' looks descriptive but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware such as pots, tools and utensils forged from a common metal.

clue.text: Report of the Parisian district

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' (plural)
a patch is an area or district, as a policeman's patch

explanation.surface: An account of a neighbourhood in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' marks the French: des means 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is a message or news report sent from abroad.

clue.text: Frank, a pet suitor

parts.note: frank means plain, outspoken
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a tiff

explanation.surface: Frank owns an animal that wants to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but is the adjective; pet is the sulk, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor in law is one who brings a suit, the party suing in court.

clue.text: Heartless person who's well-known for speed

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: A callous famous person is known for being quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes B, the middle of the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftness of movement or action, a formal synonym for quickness.

clue.text: Dealer coughing more

definitions.meaning: the person running a casino gaming table
croupy, hoarse with croup, made comparative

explanation.surface: A card dealer with a worsening cough.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke: the comparative of croupy, suffering from croup, a children's coughing illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino employee who rakes in chips and pays out at roulette or cards.

clue.text: Ruler caught by current in Xanadu's river

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the current's letter goes inside the river's name

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river of Xanadu in Coleridge's Kubla Khan
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A ruler is swept away by the current in the river of Kubla Khan's Xanadu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside ALPH, after C. Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Muslim civil and religious leaders who succeeded Muhammad.

clue.text: Henry and John shout to attract attention

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
john and loo are both slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Two men, Henry and John, call out to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a second man's name; it is slang for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting cry urging on hounds, more generally a call to get someone's notice.

clue.text: Old composer died? That is exaggerated

parts.note: Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: Did an old composer die? That is an overstatement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Mark Twain's 'reports of my death are greatly exaggerated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Overstated or carried too far is to have taken something past reasonable limits.

clue.text: Ill-humour observed round place

indicators.note: the observed word is wrapped round the place abbreviation

parts.note: seen means observed

explanation.surface: Bad temper is noticed around the location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the observed word about the place abbreviation; 'Ill-humour' is fair because the organ was once held to be the seat of bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or bad temper, once thought to come from an abdominal organ.

clue.text: Reduce glare

definitions.meaning: to frown or scowl, rhyming with power, also spelt lour

explanation.surface: Cut down the dazzle.
explanation.walkthrough: In the second sense it rhymes with 'flower': to scowl or look threatening.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something down is to diminish it; to scowl darkly is a second, separate sense.

clue.text: Prince, for instance, has two little boys

parts.note: Roy and Al are two boys' names, short ones
Roy and Al are two boys' names, short ones

explanation.surface: A prince has a pair of small sons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two little boys' gives two short names, ROY and AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a member of the monarch's family, an example of such a person.

clue.text: Dear old wife, so thoughtful

parts.note: an ex is a former wife
pensive means thoughtful

explanation.surface: My dear former wife was so pensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Dear looks like a term of endearment; it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced, costing a lot of money.

clue.text: Showing anger that's appropriate when powerless

indicators.note: powerless means the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: to pirate is to appropriate or steal

explanation.surface: Being angry is fitting when you have no power.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate looks like the adjective 'fitting'; it is the verb 'steal'. P, for power, is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious or cross, displaying temper.

clue.text: Shared facility featured in political manifesto

definitions.meaning: a telephone line shared by several subscribers
the official policy line of a political party

explanation.surface: A communal amenity is promised in a party's election programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared telephone connection, and also a party's official policy stance.

clue.text: Heading off wonderful example of Pyrenean wild life

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: wizard is old slang for wonderful

explanation.surface: Setting off, a fine specimen of Pyrenean wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: WIZARD is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamois of the Pyrenees, a goat-antelope found in those mountains.

clue.text: Pitch for performing nocturne?

definitions.meaning: John Field, Irish composer who invented the nocturne, so performing one is a jocular sense of the phrase

explanation.surface: A tone ideal for playing a night piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks musical, beside nocturne, but it is a sports ground. John Field wrote the first nocturnes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports field or ground where games are played.
